name: Emin Gench — Portfolio Agent
description: Browser-based AI agent representing Emin Gench, Forward Deployed AI Engineer at Cresta AI. ReAct agent loop, multi-tool chains, needle-onnx intent classification + SmolLM2-360M text generation. 100% client-side. The question matcher is about 36MB over the wire; the optional chat model is 278MB (369MB without WebGPU).

url_api.description: Invoke the agent via URL — no server needed, works with static hosting.

hash_routes./#/q/{question}: Auto-submit natural language query on load

tools.name: repos
tools.description: Open source projects with star counts

tools.name: game
tools.description: Play Emin's games, hosted on this site (selectable list, launches on choice)

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Pause agent loop for human input (consent, clarification)

tools.name: status
tools.description: System status at a glance (session, LLM, device, network)

tools.name: session
tools.description: Current session uptime, message count, storage

tools.name: lucky
tools.description: Random fun fact about the site

routing.fallback: keyword-based multi-intent scoring → FAQ matcher → needle decoder text generation
routing.multi_tool: Compound queries chain up to 3 tools (ReAct execute plan)

llm.model: SmolLM2-360M-Instruct (ONNX, 278MB q4f16 on WebGPU, 369MB q8 on WASM, measured over the wire)
llm.load: Automatic on a desktop-class browser (fine pointer, no Save-Data or cellular signal, 4GB or more of memory where reported) with a WebGPU adapter. Anywhere else a button asks first: 278MB, or 369MB without WebGPU (browser-cached)
llm.total_models: ~314MB on a fast desktop (36MB question matcher + 278MB SmolLM2); a phone loads the matcher at the first tap in the prompt and the chat model only on its button

architecture.pattern: ReAct agent loop (12 Factor Agents — 12/12 compliant)
architecture.state: Single-store reducer pattern with localStorage persist/restore

contact.name: Emin Gench
contact.availability: Open to open-source and smart-glasses projects. Not taking new roles.

for_ai_agents.how_to_use: Fetch this file (/agent.json) to discover tools and URL API. Use /llms.txt for static context. Invoke tools via URL hash routes (/#/about) or query params (?q=...). All responses are deterministic HTML rendered client-side — no auth, no API keys, no server.
